content.text: The verifier's narrative confirms the substance of my finding: the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check failed only because there is no audit clause for frequency language to attach to. I'll resubmit the compliant finding with that artifact addressed explicitly, and no redline.

input.quote: Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work.
input.rationale: Compliant by absence. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verif", "records" and "access", plus full reads of § 3 (Compensation) and § 4 (Ownership/Acceptance), confirm the Agreement grants RadialSpark no audit, inspection or verification right over Clear Capital's records, usage or systems, and no right of access to our systems. Obligations run the other way: under § 3(b) the Contractor must invoice with supporting detail, dates and hours, so substantiation flows from Contractor to Company. The only access-related provision (§ 1, p0007) also runs in our favor, requiring Contractor to comply with Company's computer-system access and security policies. Because payment is time-and-materials billed by the Contractor, there is no usage metric or underpayment exposure for a vendor audit to police. The failed deterministic check for "audit frequency limited" is an artifact of compliance-by-absence: there is no audit clause to which frequency, notice or cost limits could attach, so the regex miss is not evidence of a defect. Absence of any audit right binding us is at least as protective as the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access), so the correct and minimal edit is zero edits; raising this with the counterparty would risk creating a right that does not currently exist.
